payload.reason: The evidence explains that prior knowledge distillation techniques are ineffective for producing student models with different vocabularies because they require the teacher and student models to share the same vocabulary and output space, which is not the case when vocabularies differ. This leads to misalignment in tokenization and output predictions, making it challenging to transfer knowledge effectively.

claims.text: Knowledge distillation techniques require the teacher and student models to share the same vocabulary, which is not possible when the vocabularies differ.
Different tokenizations between teacher and student vocabularies lead to misalignment in outputs, hindering effective knowledge transfer.
